rationale: The Latin anchor *irruere* ("to rush/burst into, to attack") and the Biblical quotation (winds rushing/bursting upon a house, Mt. 7:25) strongly indicate a sudden, forceful movement against something, which aligns best with rush.v.02 ("attack suddenly") rather than the general high-speed movement of rush.v.01 or rush.v.04. The co-occurrence of *corruere* and *decidere* (to fall/collapse) further supports a violent, impetuous onset rather than mere rapid locomotion.
